You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like late 2017. The fed funds rate near 1.16% fits the period, and the 2-year yield at 1.38% and 10-year at 2.27% are consistent with it. The VIX at 11.44 matches the very low volatility of that year.

The month is probably November or December 2017. In November 2017 the fed funds effective rate was 1.16%, and in December it was 1.30%, so November fits better. Other readings also point to November:

- The unemployment rate of 4.3% is slightly lower than the 4.1% seen in November, so the snapshot may be using a lagged value. Payrolls averaging 120k over three months is consistent with the hurricane-affected September and October figures.
- Headline CPI at 1.87% fits September 2017, which was 2.2%, or perhaps August at 1.9%. The 3m change of -0.92 suggests a drop from about 2.8% in the spring. Core CPI at 1.74% fits August or September.
- The unemployment rate of 4.3% was the reading for June, July, and August 2017. Combined with the 3m change of -0.4, it points to an earlier month.

That leaves August or September 2017. The 10-year yield at 2.27% and 2-year at 1.38% fit September better, with the 10-year at 2.33% and the 2-year at 1.44%. For August the 10-year was 2.12% and the 2-year was 1.33%, so those figures are close but not as good a match. The fed funds rate was 1.15% in both August and September 2017.

Gold fell 2.2% over the month, which fits September, when gold dropped from 1,320 to 1,280. Emerging-market equity was up only slightly over the month, and the 7-10y Treasuries were down 0.5%, which also suits September. The dollar was weak year over year, which also fits.

September 2017 is my best guess.
